content.title: About
content.content: Red homemade salsa is a sauce made from ripe tomatoes, fresh onion, garlic, chili peppers, lime juice, and aromatic herbs. It has a bright, slightly spicy flavor and a rich aroma, perfect for Mexican dishes, snacks, and grilled foods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally salsa is made without added vinegar, preserving the natural freshness of the vegetables.
The red color comes from ripe tomatoes and sometimes a touch of paprika.
Salsa can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week, but its flavor is best within the first 2‑3 days.
In Mexico, "salsa fresca" refers to a fresh, uncooked version of the sauce.
Homemade salsa can contain probiotics if fermented ingredients like sauerkraut are added.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes in salsa provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and skin.

items.title: Vitamin C source
items.content: Lime and tomatoes deliver a high amount of vitamin C, boosting the immune system.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: Salsa is low in calories, making it an excellent addition to weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Onion and tomatoes add fiber, aiding digestion.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory compounds
items.content: Garlic and chili contain compounds that help reduce inflammation.

items.title: Spicy food
items.content: The chili content may irritate the stomach of people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes or onion.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added, monitor the amount, especially for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial contamination; keep refrigerated and use clean utensils.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve salsa with nachos, tacos, burritos, grilled meat, fish, or vegetable dishes. It can be used as a marinade, mixed into salads, or enjoyed as a fresh dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store salsa in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors or changes color.
